text:
Maya Chen: Customer (acct: ac-8892) opened CS-7124 — invoice shows 189 tokens but their SDK estimator reports ~120. They pasted a curl response header with x-metering info, asking why ~60 tokens missing.
Ethan Brooks: Thanks — can you paste the request payload they used? streaming vs non-streaming matters here.
Maya Chen: Pasted below from customer: they call our completions streaming endpoint with a system message + user prompt + a function/tool call that returns a JSON blob from an external tool. They used the JS SDK estimateTokenCount helper before send, got 118-123 depending on run.
Sam — Support: MeteringBot attached an automated note: Ticket CS-7124 created and escalated to eng-metering. :rotating_light:
MeteringBot: server_meter_report: tokens=189, model=redwood-v2, session=se-42a
Priya Patel: Quick theory — our SDK estimator currently omits server-injected assistant messages that are added during streaming (toolcall preamble or canonicalization). If the tool returns a JSON with long keys, the server may append an assistant role message with that tool output which the client never saw at estimate time.
Ethan Brooks: That fits. Customer's curl shows this header in the final response:```HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
x-redwood-metering-tokens: 189
x-redwood-invoice-id: inv-2026-08-12-99
```They also included the streaming websocket transcript where an assistant tool_call chunk arrives after the SDK's estimator finished.
Maya Chen: Customer included a minimal repro. Here's the payload they used (sanitized):```json
{
  "model": "redwood-v2",
  "messages": [
    {"role":"system","content":"You are an analyzer."},
    {"role":"user","content":"Summarize attached data"},
    {"role":"assistant","name":"tool.xfetch","content":"(tool call)"}
  ],
  "stream": true
}
```They claim estimateTokenCount(messages) -> 121, invoice header -> 189.
Priya Patel: Another angle — tokenizer differences for non-visible control bytes or escaped unicode from tool output. If the tool returns escaped unicode or long structured JSON, server-side canonicalization can expand strings (e.g., pretty-printed or with extra metadata) which increases token count. The SDK estimator runs before the tool executes so it never counts that server-side expansion.
Ethan Brooks: Repro suggestion: run the same call non-streaming so tool output is present in the response body at estimate time and compare SDK estimator vs final metering header. Also capture the server-side metering header (`x-redwood-metering-tokens`) from the real API.
Maya Chen: Customer tried non-streaming and saw estimator=120 vs header=187 still. They attached the server body:```json
{"id":"resp-1","choices":[{"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"{\"extracted\":\"lots of keys and long strings\"}"}}],"usage":{"total_tokens":189}}
```They said SDK didn't count the assistant's tool output string.
Priya Patel: Okay actionable root cause hypothesis: the SDK's estimate helper ignores the assistant/tool name payload that is synthesized by the server when we convert tool outputs into assistant messages. Two contributing factors: streaming timing (estimate runs before tool output exists) and canonicalization (server transforms tool raw output into a different tokenizable representation).
Ethan Brooks: Quick check — can you ask the customer to add `X-Redwood-Debug: include-server-token-report` to the request so we can compare stepwise metering we emit? We can also ask them to toggle `stream=false` and attach the full response body; they already did but include raw server report.
Sam — Support: Customer replied and included raw header and body — I attached to CS-7124. They added that they use SDK v0.9.1.
Priya Patel: Note: we shipped a patch in SDK v0.9.3 that updates estimateTokenCount to optionally simulate server canonicalization for tool outputs (flag: include_server_tool_output=true). If the customer upgrades and re-runs, should get closer.
Maya Chen: I'll ask them to try v0.9.3 and to set the new flag. Also ask them to run a deterministic reproducible script:```bash
# reproduce locally
node repro.js --stream=false --sdk-version=0.9.3 --include-server-tool-output
# OR curl to capture header
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "X-Redwood-Debug: include-server-token-report" -d '@payload.json' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions
```
Ethan Brooks: I'll add an engineering task to verify server canonicalization logs for CS-7124 and to ensure our metering header matches usage baked into invoices. If server does canonicalize, we should either emit a pre-canonicalized token estimate via header or document the delta clearly.
Priya Patel: TL;DR for support: likely not a billing bug (customer still charged correct server count) — it's an estimator blind spot around server-side tool output canonicalization + streaming. Action items: 1) ask customer to upgrade SDK 0.9.3 and enable flag, 2) capture `x-redwood-metering-tokens` and response body, 3) eng to audit CS-7124 canonicalization path.
Sam — Support: Passed to customer with repro steps and link to patch notes. Customer asked for a temporary workaround to avoid surprises; suggested `stream=false` and post-process tool outputs client-side if they want local counts.
Maya Chen: I'll follow up after customer tries v0.9.3. Marking thread resolved for now but leaving CS-7124 open until eng confirms logs. :white_check_mark:
